question: Which of the following is the second highest post in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (09/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: President
Prime Minister
Vice President
Governor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vice President

Explanation:
According to the Indian Constitution, the President is the highest constitutional post in the country. The Vice President is the second highest post, coming after the President. The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and performs the duties of the President in their absence. The Prime Minister is the head of the government but ranks below the Vice President in the constitutional order. The Governor is the constitutional head of a state and ranks lower than the Vice President at the national level. Therefore, the second highest post is the Vice President.

question: Who has the power to declare a national emergency in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (09/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Supreme Court
Union Cabinet
Prime Minister
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
Under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to declare a national emergency. This emergency can be proclaimed on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. The President exercises this power only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet, headed by the Prime Minister. The proclamation must be approved by both houses of Parliament within one month. It can remain in force indefinitely, but requires parliamentary approval every six months. During a national emergency, the federal structure becomes unitary, with the central government gaining authority to issue directions to states. Fundamental Rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended, and other rights can be suspended under Article 359. The President's role is crucial as the constitutional head, ensuring the decision is based on cabinet advice.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What happens to Fundamental Rights during national emergency? → They can be suspended under Article 359
☛ How many times has national emergency been imposed in India? → Three times (1962, 1971, 1975)
☛ What is the effect of national emergency on state governments? → Central government can issue directions to states
☛ Does Parliament review the national emergency? → Yes, every six months

question: How many times has the financial emergency been declared in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (09/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Never
2 times
1 time
3 times
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Never

Explanation:
Under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to declare a financial emergency if the financial stability of the country is threatened. As of 2024, a financial emergency has never been declared in India. Unlike the national emergency (Article 352) and President's rule in states (Article 356), the financial emergency has never been invoked. Under this provision, the central government can interfere in the financial matters of states, impose salary cuts, and suspend financial provisions. The financial emergency remains a dormant provision in the Indian Constitution.

question: How many topics are currently there in India's Union List? (RPF Constable 2018 (09/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: 100 Topics
97 topics
52 topics
47 topics
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 100 Topics

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Union List includes subjects on which only the central government can legislate, such as defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, etc. Originally, the Union List had 97 subjects, but through amendments, it has been increased to 100 subjects. This increase was mainly due to the addition of new subjects like central forces, human organ transplantation, etc. Currently, the Union List has 100 subjects, the State List has 61 subjects, and the Concurrent List has 52 subjects.

question: In the year ____, the word 'integrity' was added in the preamble of the Indian Constitution. (RPF Constable 2018 (09/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: 1966
1986
1956
1976
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1976

Explanation:
The word 'integrity' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution in 1976 by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment. This amendment also added the words 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble. Before this amendment, the Preamble described India as a 'sovereign', 'democratic', 'republic'. The 42nd Amendment is the most comprehensive amendment to the Indian Constitution, often called the 'Mini-Constitution'. It also introduced the Fundamental Duties. The term 'integrity' emphasizes the unity and integrity of the nation.

☛ Which amendment introduced Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Amendment

question: The term of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is for __________. (RPF Constable 2018 (09/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Seven Years
Four years
Five years
Six years
solution:

The CAG acts as the guardian of India's public financial system and audits government accounts.

question: During the British rule, under which act was the establishment of a Dyarchy system in the Indian provinces? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: Government of India Act 1919
Indian Councils Act 1909
Government of India Act 1935
Charter Act 1833
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act 1919

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, introduced the Dyarchy system in the provinces. Under this system, provincial subjects were divided into Reserved and Transferred categories. Reserved subjects like police, justice, and finance were controlled by the Governor, while transferred subjects like education, health, and local self-government were given to ministers responsible to the provincial legislature. This system aimed at gradual constitutional progress but was largely unsuccessful. The act also established a bicameral legislature at the centre and extended communal representation.

question: Which of the following article related to the Indian Constitution is concerned with the ancillary powers of the Supreme Court? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: Article 238
Article 143
Article 243
Article 140
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 140

Explanation:
Article 140 of the Indian Constitution deals with the ancillary powers of the Supreme Court. This article empowers Parliament to confer by law supplemental powers on the Supreme Court as may be necessary for the effective exercise of its functions. It enables the Court to make such orders as are necessary for doing complete justice and to ensure proper administration of justice. Article 140 is part of the provisions regarding the Supreme Court's powers and jurisdiction (Articles 124-147). It allows the Court to exercise powers that are incidental or ancillary to its main functions, aiding in the enforcement of its decrees and orders. This article strengthens the judiciary's role as the guardian of the Constitution by providing the Court with necessary auxiliary powers to uphold the rule of law.

question: Which of the following is not a constitutional institution? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Union Public Service Commission
National Scheduled Tribes Commission
National Human Rights Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Human Rights Commission

Explanation:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is a statutory body, not a constitutional one. It was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. In contrast, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Union Public Service Commission, and National Commission for Scheduled Tribes are constitutional institutions as they are directly mentioned in the Indian Constitution. Article 338 pertains to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Article 315 to the Union Public Service Commission, and Article 338A to the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. NHRC is crucial for the protection and promotion of human rights but is created by an Act of Parliament rather than the Constitution itself.

question: Who chairs the joint sitting of both the houses of the house? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: Chief Minister
Speaker of Lok Sabha
Prime Minister
Rajya Sabha Speaker
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Speaker of Lok Sabha

Explanation:
As per Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of Lok Sabha chairs the joint sitting of both houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Such a sitting is convened when a bill passed by one house is pending in the other house for more than six months, or the other house rejects it or proposes amendments. The President summons the joint sitting. If the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha presides. Decisions in a joint sitting are taken by a simple majority of the total members present. So far, three joint sittings have been held in India: the Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), the POTA Bill (1978), and the Women's Reservation Bill (2008).

question: According to the Indian Constitution, the maximum number of members of Rajya Sabha has been fixed______. (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: 250
380
150
368
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 250

Explanation:
According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum number of members of Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250. Out of these, 238 members represent states and union territories, elected indirectly, and 12 members are nominated by the President. These nominated members have special knowledge in fields like literature, science, art, and social service. Currently, the strength of Rajya Sabha is 245, as 5 seats out of 250 are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved, but one-third of its members retire every two years. This structure ensures continuity in the legislative process, with members serving a six-year term. The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

question: What is the "minimum number of required members in the House before editing any work" called? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: Quorum
Membership
Organization
Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Quorum

Explanation:
Quorum is the minimum number of members required to be present in a house or meeting before any business can be transacted. According to Article 100 of the Indian Constitution, at least one-tenth of the total membership must be present in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to constitute a quorum. If the quorum is not met, the presiding officer can adjourn the house. The term 'quorum' is derived from Latin, meaning 'of whom'. It is a crucial aspect of legislative procedure ensuring adequate representation for decision-making. Decisions made in the absence of a quorum are considered invalid. Quorum guarantees that no law or resolution is passed without sufficient participation of members.

question_hi: किसी भी कार्य को संपादित करने से पहले सदन में आवश्यक सदस्यों की न्यूनतम संख्या क्या कहलाती है? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))

question: Which of the following proposals can the Council of Ministers resign? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019))
options: Attendance Resolution passed in Parliament
Slander resolution passed in Parliament
Dispute Resolution passed in Parliament
Suspension Proposal for Non-Resident Day Passed in Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dispute Resolution passed in Parliament

Explanation:
According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers on any policy or action, the Council must resign. A no-confidence motion is a dispute resolution proposal that expresses disagreement with the government's policies. Other options like Attendance Resolution, Slander Resolution, or Suspension Proposal for Non-Resident Day do not compel the Council of Ministers to resign. This provision ensures the accountability of the government in a parliamentary democracy.

question: How many fundamental duties are mentioned in the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: 11
10
8
9
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 11

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution originally had 10 fundamental duties, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. Later, the 86th Amendment (2002) added one more duty, making the total 11. These duties are listed under Part IV-A in Article 51A. They are not legally enforceable but are moral obligations for citizens. They include respecting the national flag and Constitution, defending the country, promoting social harmony, protecting the environment, and developing a scientific temper. The 11th duty mandates providing educational opportunities for children aged 6-14.

question: Which of the following has been described in the eleventh part of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Union Territory
Emergency Provisions
Election
Relationship between center and states
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Relationship between center and states

Explanation:
Part XI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 245 to 263) describes the relationship between the center and states. It covers legislative, administrative, and financial relations. Articles 245-255 deal with legislative relations, defining the division of powers between Parliament and state legislatures. Articles 256-263 cover administrative relations, including the power of the center to give directions to states. Financial relations are described in Part XII. Union Territories are covered in Part VIII, Emergency Provisions in Part XVIII, and Elections in Part XV. Thus, Part XI exclusively focuses on center-state relations.

question: Which is the only state in India that has its separate constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Nagaland
Karnataka
Sikkim
Jammu and Kashmir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jammu and Kashmir

Explanation:
Under Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, Jammu and Kashmir had a special status that allowed it to have its own separate constitution. This constitution was adopted in 1956 and governed the internal affairs of the state. On August 5, 2019, Article 370 was abrogated, revoking the special status of Jammu and Kashmir, and the state was divided into two Union Territories. Other states like Nagaland, Karnataka, and Sikkim do not have their separate constitutions; they are governed under the provisions of the Indian Constitution.

question: Who appoints the Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Delhi? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019) Shift 2)

Chief Justice of the High Court
President of India
Neighborhood Governor
solution:

Explanation:
Delhi is a Union Territory with a special status as the National Capital Territory (NCT). Under Article 239AA of the Constitution, the Chief Minister of Delhi is appointed by the President of India. The President acts through the Lieutenant Governor (the Governor of Delhi). The Chief Minister must prove majority in the Delhi Legislative Assembly. This process is similar to other states where the Governor appoints the Chief Minister, but in Delhi's case, the appointment is directly by the President due to its status as a Union Territory. This provision makes Delhi unique as a Union Territory with a legislature.

question: Which of the following is related to the abolition of titles in the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Article 24
Article 18
Article 51
Article 21A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 18

Explanation:
Article 18 of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of titles. It falls under the Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35) and specifically under the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18). Article 18 prohibits the state from conferring any titles on citizens and also prohibits Indian citizens from accepting titles from foreign states. However, military and academic distinctions are exempted from this provision. This article ensures equality among citizens and abolishes feudal practices. Other options: Article 24 relates to prohibition of child labour, Article 51 pertains to promotion of international peace, and Article 21A deals with the right to education.

question: The Indian Constitution has the tendency of the directive principles of the policy of the state- (RPF Constable 2018 (10/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Establishment of Political Republic
Judicial
Police State Concept
Non-justiciable
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Non-justiciable

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are mentioned in Part IV of the Indian Constitution. These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by any court. They serve as guidelines for the government in policy-making but are not legally binding. Article 37 states that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, yet they are not enforceable by any court. This characteristic distinguishes DPSP from Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable. The aim of DPSP is to establish social and economic democracy, such as equal pay for equal work, organization of village panchayats, and right to education. The DPSP were inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to create a welfare state. The 42nd Amendment (1976) gave primacy to DPSP over Fundamental Rights in certain cases.

☛ From which constitution is DPSP borrowed? → Ireland
☛ What is the objective of DPSP? → To establish a welfare state
☛ How many articles are in DPSP? → 36 to 51 (total 16)
☛ Which article distinguishes DPSP from Fundamental Rights? → Article 37
☛ Which amendment gave primacy to DPSP? → 42nd Amendment (1976)

options_hi: राजनीतिक गणतंत्र की स्थापना

पुलिस राज्य अवधारणा

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है वाद योग्य नहीं

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निदेशक सिद्धांत (DPSP) का उल्लेख है। ये सिद्धांत किसी भी न्यायालय में वाद योग्य नहीं हैं, अर्थात इन्हें लागू करने के लिए न्यायालय में मुकदमा नहीं किया जा सकता। ये सरकार के लिए नीति-निर्माण में मार्गदर्शक हैं, लेकिन कानूनी रूप से बाध्यकारी नहीं। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, ये सिद्धांत देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं, फिर भी ये न्यायालयों द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय नहीं हैं। यह विशेषता DPSP को मौलिक अधिकारों से अलग करती है, जो वाद योग्य हैं। DPSP का उद्देश्य सामाजिक और आर्थिक लोकतंत्र स्थापित करना है, जैसे समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन, ग्राम पंचायतों का संगठन, और शिक्षा का अधिकार।

Explanation:
भारत में केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में लेफ्टिनेंट गवर्नर और प्रशासकों की नियुक्ति गृह मंत्रालय के अंतर्गत आती है। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 239 के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति प्रत्येक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के लिए एक प्रशासक नियुक्त करता है, जो गृह मंत्रालय की सिफारिश पर किया जाता है। यह मंत्रालय केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन, सुरक्षा और नीति निर्धारण के लिए जिम्मेदार है। गृह मंत्रालय का प्रमुख गृह मंत्री होता है। इस प्रकार, लेफ्टिनेंट गवर्नर और प्रशासकों की नियुक्ति गृह मंत्रालय के माध्यम से होती है।

solution:

Explanation:
